title: Rework rerank IO format and incremental results for latency-sensitive flows
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Current rerank endpoint mixes full-result blocking responses, unclear top_k semantics for ties, and an opaque continuation token. High-volume customers and latency-sensitive frontends want an ergonomic API that: 1) supports incremental/streaming delivery of partial rerank results, 2) defines deterministic top_k semantics (stable tie-breaking, consistent ordering across pagination), and 3) accepts both raw text and precomputed embeddings without ambiguous schema rules. This ticket defines the I/O contract changes and implements server-side support for incremental result windows to reduce tail latency and memory pressure.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts combined payloads: candidates (ids + optional embeddings) and query (text or embedding) with explicit 'input_type' field

Top_k parameter semantics documented: k is the maximum number of returned high-confidence items; tie-breaking deterministic by (score, candidate_id) with option 'stable=false' for legacy non-deterministic ordering
Streaming/incremental mode: clients can set 'window_size' and receive partial ranked windows via chunked transfer (or websocket) with stable continuation tokens between windows

Pagination token contract: token is opaque but stable across retries for the same model+checkpoint; token contains server-side cursor version id to enable safe rollbacks and reject incompatible rollouts
Benchmarked: P95 latency reduced by 20% for large candidate payloads when using windowed streaming compared to full-blocking rerank
Backward compatibility: existing clients without 'window_size' get full blocking response with original field names for 3 release cycles
implementation_notes: Schema: add 'input_type': 'text'|'embedding' and 'candidates': [{id, metadata?, embedding?}] to disambiguate client intent
Server: implement streaming layer that emits ranked windows of size N; backend performs coarse-grained prefilter scoring (cheap vector dot) then final expensive model rerank on window
Tie-breaking: use lexicographic (score desc, candidate_id asc) by default to guarantee deterministic stable ordering across pages
Continuation tokens: include opaque base64 blob with server cursor id + checksum; server validates token version to detect model rollouts and return HTTP 409 with guidance when incompatible
Fallback: if client provides embeddings and server has embedding model mismatch, compute server-side projection and set warning in response metadata
Telemetry: add counters and histograms for window sizes, number of windows per request, token validation failures, and rollback events
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated: start behind 'rerank_incremental' feature flag for staging and internal canaries
Canary: route 5% of production traffic for 72h with synthetic workload that simulates 10k candidate rerank requests
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% over 4 weeks with SLA checkpoints at each step
Fallback policy: on token validation errors or model incompatibility return structured error with code 'RK_TOKEN_INCOMPATIBLE' and fallback to full blocking rerank if caller opts in
Docs & SDKs: release updated SDK (python/js) that exposes 'window_size', 'input_type', and streaming helper; deprecate old pagination param after 3 releases
qa_plan: Unit tests for deterministic tie-break ordering across seeds and pagination boundaries
Integration tests: replay recorded customer workloads with and without precomputed embeddings to assert parity
Load test: synthetic candidate sets up to 50k items to measure P95/P99 latency with windowed vs blocking modes
Chaos test: simulate model rollout where continuation tokens become invalid mid-request and assert correct 409 behavior and metrics emission
Security test: ensure continuation token validation prevents token forging and does not leak internal cursor IDs
